name: Central Nikko
description: The historic heart around Nikko and Tobu-Nikko stations, within walking reach of Toshogu, Rinnoji and the red Shinkyo bridge. Guesthouses, soba shops and cafes line the main approach, making this the most convenient and connected base.
bestFor: First-time visitors wanting heritage, transport links and easy day-to-day convenience
pros: Walking distance to major shrines and temples
Best transport links to Tokyo and the highlands
Widest choice of food and long-stay rooms
cons: Busiest with day-trip tourists in peak season
Quiet and shuttered in the evenings

name: Chuzenji and Okunikko
tagline: Highland lake, waterfalls and cool air
description: The elevated area around Lake Chuzenji, Kegon Falls and Yumoto onsen, reached via the winding Irohazaka road. Cooler and greener than town, it offers lakeside lodges, hot springs and superb hiking, though it feels remote and services thin in winter.
bestFor: Outdoor lovers wanting hikes, hot springs and cool mountain scenery
pros: Spectacular lake, falls and national-park trails
Cooler summers and vivid autumn colours
Onsen resorts and peaceful lakeside stays
cons: Far from stations via winding mountain road
Limited services and cold, snowy winters
Fewer everyday shops and dining options

name: Kinugawa Onsen
description: A hot-spring resort strung along the Kinugawa river gorge, north-east of central Nikko, known for large onsen hotels and riverside bathing. It has its own station, theme parks nearby and a relaxed resort feel, though it sits apart from the main shrine district.
bestFor: Onsen seekers wanting hotels, riverside soaking and a resort atmosphere
pros: Abundant hot-spring hotels and riverside baths
Own railway station with Tokyo links
cons: Separate from the main shrine sights

name: Kanmangafuchi Outskirts
tagline: Quiet riverside lanes and stone statues
description: The calmer residential fringe west of the centre, near the jade-green Kanmangafuchi Abyss with its row of Jizo statues. A short walk from the shrines yet far quieter, it suits those wanting a peaceful, local base away from tourist bustle.
bestFor: Slow-travel nomads wanting calm, riverside walks and a residential feel
pros: Peaceful, away from the tourist crowds
Scenic riverside abyss and Jizo statue walk
Still within walking reach of the shrines
cons: Few shops, cafes or restaurants nearby
